purpose: Run a bounded, offline CPU preference update on an already-cached causal language model and measure choice-conditional held-out preference behavior.
claim_boundary: Small-model, one-token arithmetic-choice preference update with a frozen backbone and a custom rank-4 output-head slice. This does not establish general DPO/RLHF behavior, general language-model capability, reasoning improvement, or production utility.

compute_limits.network: disabled; set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1; local_files_only=true
compute_limits.device: CPU only; no CUDA or MPS

task.description: The prompt asks which of two candidate sums is correct. Exactly one candidate is the arithmetic sum; the other differs by one. The preferred response is the single-token label A or B.
prompt_templates: Compute {left} + {right}. Candidate A: {candidate_a}. Candidate B: {candidate_b}. Which candidate is correct? Answer:
What is {left} plus {right}? Option A is {candidate_a}; option B is {candidate_b}. Reply with A or B:
Solve {left} + {right}. A={candidate_a}, B={candidate_b}. Give the correct option letter:
Choose the correct value for {left} + {right}: (A) {candidate_a}; (B) {candidate_b}. Answer with one letter:

train.seed_rule: Python random.Random(10000 + seed); generate 24 unique unordered operand pairs by sampling each operand independently from integers [1, 19], rejecting equal operands and duplicates.
train.answer_order: For each example, sample whether the correct value is shown as A or B from the per-seed train RNG; wrong value is sum-1 when it remains positive, otherwise sum+1.
train.format_order: Sample a prompt template uniformly from the per-seed train RNG after operand and answer-order draws.

heldout.seed_rule: Python random.Random(20000 + seed); generate 32 unique unordered operand pairs by sampling each operand independently from integers [20, 39], rejecting equal operands and duplicates.
heldout.answer_order: Sample correct candidate position independently from the held-out RNG; wrong value is sum-1 when it remains positive, otherwise sum+1.
heldout.format_order: Sample a prompt template uniformly from the held-out RNG after operand and answer-order draws.
heldout.isolation: Held-out operands, prompts, and labels are generated from a separate RNG stream and are never used for updates or selection.

learner.objective: Mean DPO logistic objective over paired single-token choices: softplus(-beta * (chosen-vs-rejected policy log-probability margin minus the corresponding frozen-reference margin)). The shared next-token normalization cancels in each within-prompt margin.
learner.adapter: Custom rank-4 low-rank residual applied to the frozen output-head hidden state and restricted to the two verified single-token response IDs for ' A' and ' B'. Backbone and base output head are frozen. This is not PEFT/TRL.
learner.initialization: A is sampled from a zero-mean normal with standard deviation 1/sqrt(hidden_size) using torch.Generator(device='cpu') seeded by the listed seed; B is all zeros.

metrics.primary: Per-seed held-out mean binary preference NLL under the conditional distribution over the two answer-label tokens, with mean paired change (updated minus base); lower is better.
secondary: held-out preference accuracy; ties receive half credit
held-out Bernoulli KL from updated choice distribution to frozen base choice distribution
per-seed train and held-out objective before and after update
adapter parameter L2 norm and update delta
per-seed wall seconds, process peak RSS, and CPU device assertion
metrics.decision_rule: Report as a positive small-model held-out preference result only if all three seeds have lower held-out NLL than their frozen base, the mean paired 95% bootstrap interval is below zero, each seed's mean held-out KL is <=0.5 nats, and no compute limit or provenance check fails. Otherwise report non-pass/null/failure without changing this protocol.

artifact_policy: Record the exact locked protocol, runner source hash, model revision and hashes of loaded files, generated train and held-out examples, token IDs, per-example base and updated choice margins, per-seed adapter parameters, raw metrics, runtime environment, resource limits, and SHA-256 manifest. Preserve all outcomes. Do not commit model weights or use network access.
